rationale: Diagnostic cohort before inspecting any warehouse-specific held-out arrival curve: first seven observed days provide one weekly cycle for training-only warehouse selection; next three days are reserved calibration context and remaining complete source bins held out. Three calibration days cannot justify a finite 90% daily-block conformal bound; no such claim is made. Select maximum training arrivals with numeric-ID tie break for a non-sparse diagnostic, not proof that its offered rate fits worker3. One-minute counts align with existing one-/five-minute host observation scales; preserve original UTC timestamps and raw IDs, exclude only the incomplete global final bin from count evaluation while retaining all exact arrivals. No time compression, load thinning/scaling, SQL/resource-profile mapping, intensity normalization or model fit. Source-wide boundaries are observed arrival metadata, not selected-warehouse outcome tuning. CPU/memory limits are offline operational limits, not policy parameters. Empty bins mean no reported arrivals in the supplied observation interval, not proof of server idleness or logger completeness.
